02 / A WORKFLOW YOU CAN REPEAT

Drop. Choose. Convert.

01

Bring your files

Drop multiple files into a batch, or select a folder to create a ZIP. Batches support up to 256 entries.

02

Choose a compatible target

Mixed batches show formats supported by every input. A readiness check flags missing engines and fidelity warnings before work begins.

03

Keep the result where you want it

Save beside the originals or choose an output folder. Auto-rename, skip, or explicitly overwrite existing files.

More control
when you need it.

Adjust video quality and resolution, audio bitrate, and hardware encoder selection where supported. Cancel jobs, retry failures, and copy a batch report for troubleshooting.

03 / ON YOUR MACHINE

The files
stay with you.

Desktop conversion runs locally. File2File does not require a cloud conversion service.

The app brings a shared interface to established conversion engines and Rust-native data and archive tools. The source is available under the MIT license.

04 / BEFORE YOU START

A little setup.
Clear expectations.

File2File is the desktop interface. External conversion engines are installed separately.

Step-by-step installation guide
FFmpeg + FFprobeAudio & video
ImageMagickImages & vector rasterization
PandocDocument interchange
Poppler utilitiesPDF extraction
Built-in Rust toolsData & archives · no external engine

Engine Health identifies missing or unusable engines and disables the affected formats. The DEB declares the main runtime packages; other packages require separate setup.

Will every conversion preserve the original perfectly?

No. PDF extraction can change or lose layout, fonts, forms, and images. Document conversions may change styles. Media can lose quality when using lossy codecs. JPEG output flattens transparency onto white. XLSX conversion uses the first worksheet only.

Can it remove metadata?

Metadata stripping is available for FFmpeg media and ImageMagick image routes. It is not guaranteed for every format or document engine.

What about large files and archives?

Structured-data inputs are limited to 32 MiB, with a 128 MiB expanded XLSX limit. Archives are limited to 10,000 entries and 5 GiB of expanded data. Links and special files are excluded. See the documentation for the complete safety limits.

Is there a browser version?

The repository includes a limited browser fallback for lightweight transformations. It does not provide the desktop FFmpeg, ImageMagick, Pandoc, or GPU pipeline. This website is a guide to the desktop app.
